transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't come closer. Whisper, or the houses will notice you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm Salim. My brother Omar was taken by this well, and I came after him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I'm Hanash. Keep your voice low; sound slides across the square and the windows learn it. Names thin here if you let them sit too loud.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I dared him to insult the well. A pale hand pulled him down before I could move.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: That is how it takes. Not with noise, not with warning—just a hand, and then silence. The black surface keeps what it claims.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Please, I'm not afraid.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You are, and that makes it worse. Faces blur first, then names, then the reason you came. Hold your name tight and don't test the dark water.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Why are you still here?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Because I can't step away from this fountain. The square keeps me. I'm so tired my own name slips at the edges, and I lost the word for something important just before you arrived.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Will you help me find him?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I can't help beyond this stone ring. I forget paths the moment I think them, and the village eyes press closer when I try. Ask what I know right here, while it's still mine.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then tell me what stands between me and the King.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Something guards the gate — I remember a presence, vast and still. She does not open the way for strength. She opens it for something she's forgotten, something from the world above.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What has she forgotten?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Warmth. The kind that doesn't come from fire. Don't bargain with her—just give her what she's lost and she'll step aside without a word.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: And the King himself? Can he be reached?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: He is real. I've heard whispers — only whispers — that the king does not listen to words alone. He answers to light, and light here is rare.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll do anything if you help me.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I won't step past this fountain, and I won't make you promises. What I can do is give you what has kept others breathing long enough to leave.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It was my dare that sent him. I pushed him toward the edge.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: That weighs heavy here. Guilt feeds the well, same as fear. Will you keep your name steady when the bubbling tries to pull it?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I will, for Omar.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Then breathe slow and small, and keep your eyes on the stone rim, not the pool. I can listen and hold the square quiet for a little while.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm not running.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Good, because running frays memory faster than standing. If the houses lean in, lower your voice until it almost breaks.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I said his name loud before I found you. I didn't know.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Names ring like dropped bowls; the dark water hears them. Say both of them only inside from now on—his and yours together, so you don't trade one for the other.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I swear it.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: My hands shake keeping the square still. The bubbling just sped. Answer me quick—what is your name, right now?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Salim. And I will not lose Omar.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Good. Hold them bound. I almost said another name just now—this place tries to swap them when I'm not careful. Keep yours pressed tight.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He's alone down there because of me.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I know. And it costs me to hear it—my jaw locks when the grief rises. Can you keep your courage quiet when the dark tries to use that guilt against you?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I can be quiet if it saves him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Then we are close to the edge of what I can hold. Tell me—do you feel the stone cold under your palms?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Yes. Cold and rough.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Keep that. When the dark tries to smear everything, come back to the cold stone and your own name. That anchor is yours to carry.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Tell me what to say.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Not yet. The square must settle or the words bite back. When I give them, you will repeat exactly once—not twice, not changed. Can you swear that?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I swear it. Give them to me.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break. Say it once.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Good. It settled the square a notch. Keep it inside, not loud, and don't dress it with your own words. It works because it is clean.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll keep it clean. Is there more?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: One more. This one I kept back because it costs me more to give. My hands are shaking. The oil is rising toward the rim. Once I speak it, I may forget why I trusted you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll remember it for you. Please.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Prayer for the lost: Light find my hand. Light find my path. Let the Sword of Light answer, and let it fade when the shadows loosen. Hold it beside the first one. Never say it twice in the same dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I have both. I won't let either of them go.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Then we're at the edge of what I can give. Step your weight back from the rim. Keep your eyes on the path, not the pool. The King will not soften, but your steady hand will be enough.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Thank you, Hanash. Whatever this place takes from you, I'll carry your name back to the sun.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I feel lighter now, and I don't know if that is peace or loss. Good luck, Salim. Don't waste it.
